capsuleTopic.title: Tree of Life
capsuleTopic.subtitle: Garden · wisdom · water · fruit · healing · access
capsuleTopic.orientation: Trace the named Tree of Life from Eden through wisdom sayings and future visions, while keeping nearby tree, vine, river, and cross images distinct.
capsuleTopic.trailPrompt: Follow where the tree appears, what surrounds it, who may approach it, and how the same phrase changes across different sources.

passages.excerpt: “For, behold, I create new heavens and a new earth; and the former things will not be remembered, nor come into mind. But be glad and rejoice forever in that which I create; for, behold…
passages.observation: The LORD promises new heavens and earth, joy in Jerusalem, long life, houses, vineyards, tree-like days, answered prayer, and peace on the holy mountain.

passages.title: The king of Tyre is addressed with Eden imagery
passages.excerpt: Moreover the LORD’s word came to me, saying, “Son of man, take up a lamentation over the king of Tyre, and tell him, ‘The Lord GOD says: “You were the seal of full measure, full of wisd…
passages.observation: A lament places the king of Tyre in Eden, describes created beauty and a guardian cherub, and narrates profanation and expulsion.

passages.title: A great tree among Eden’s trees falls
passages.excerpt: In the eleventh year, in the third month, in the first day of the month, the LORD’s word came to me, saying, “Son of man, tell Pharaoh king of Egypt and his multitude: ‘Whom are you lik…
passages.observation: The oracle compares Assyria with a water-fed cedar above other trees, places it among Eden’s trees, and narrates pride, cutting, death, and descent.

passages.title: Temple water gives life and healing fruit
passages.excerpt: He brought me back to the door of the temple; and behold, waters flowed out from under the threshold of the temple eastward, for the front of the temple faced toward the east. The water…
passages.observation: Water flows from the temple, deepens, heals the sea, supports many trees, and gives monthly fruit and leaves for healing.

passages.title: Healing is pictured through roots, shade, and fruit
passages.excerpt: “I will heal their waywardness. I will love them freely; for my anger is turned away from them. I will be like the dew to Israel. He will blossom like the lily, and send down his roots…
passages.observation: The LORD promises to heal Israel, compares renewed Israel with lily, olive, grain, and vine, and says that Ephraim’s fruit is found from him.

passages.title: Living waters flow from the reigning city
passages.excerpt: It will happen in that day that there will not be light, cold, or frost. It will be a unique day which is known to the LORD—not day, and not night; but it will come to pass that at even…
passages.observation: Zechariah describes a unique day, living waters flowing east and west from Jerusalem, the LORD as king over all the earth, and the city dwelling securely.

passages.title: Wisdom grows like trees and invites eating
passages.excerpt: I took root in a people that was honored, even in the portion of the Lord’s own inheritance. I was exalted like a cedar in Lebanon, And like a cypress tree on the mountains of Hermon. I…
passages.observation: Wisdom says she took root among an honored people, compares herself with several trees and a vine, and invites those who desire her to eat her fruits.

passages.title: Kindness and fear are gardens of blessing
passages.excerpt: Kindness is like a garden of blessings. Almsgiving endures forever. The life of one who labors and is content will be made sweet. He who finds a treasure is better than both. Children a…
passages.observation: A sequence weighs labor, family, friendship, counsel, and wisdom before comparing kindness and fear of the Lord with gardens of blessing.

passages.title: Israel is called to hear the commandments of life
passages.excerpt: Hear, O Israel, the commandments of life! Give ear to understand wisdom! How is it, O Israel, that you are in your enemies’ land, that you have become old in a strange country, that you…
passages.observation: Baruch calls Israel to hear wisdom, learn understanding, and ask why the people have grown old in a foreign country away from wisdom’s place.

passages.title: Those who hold wisdom fast will live
passages.excerpt: This is the book of God’s commandments and the law that endures forever. All those who hold it fast will live, but those who leave it will die. Turn, O Jacob, and take hold of it. Walk…
passages.observation: Baruch identifies wisdom with God’s commandments, says those who hold her fast will live and those who leave her will die, and calls Israel happy.

passages.title: The prepared kingdom includes the tree of life
passages.excerpt: The Lord says to Esdras, “Tell my people that I will give them the kingdom of Jerusalem, which I would have given to Israel. I will also take their glory back to myself, and give these…
passages.observation: The Lord promises Jerusalem, everlasting dwellings, the tree of life, rest from labor, and a kingdom already prepared.

passages.title: Paradise opens and the tree is planted
passages.excerpt: For many grievous miseries will fall on those who dwell in the world in the last times, because they have walked in great pride. But understand for yourself, and for those who inquire c…
passages.observation: A future scene announces opened Paradise, a planted tree of life, a built city, rest, the end of corruption, and revealed immortality.

passages.title: A father remembers a tree-of-life proverb
passages.excerpt: He used to teach you, when yet with you, the law and the prophets. He used to read to you about the slaying of Abel by Cain, the offering up of Isaac, and the imprisonment of Joseph. He…
passages.observation: A remembered teaching sequence attributes ancestral, prophetic, wisdom, and song texts to a father, including a tree-of-life saying assigned to Solomon.

passages.title: Jesus promises Paradise from the cross
passages.excerpt: One of the criminals who was hanged insulted him, saying, “If you are the Christ, save yourself and us!” But the other answered, and rebuking him said, “Don’t you even fear God, seeing…
passages.observation: One condemned man mocks Jesus, the other asks to be remembered, and Jesus promises that he will be with him in Paradise that day.

passages.title: Jesus speaks as the true vine
passages.phase: Life-giving plant images at the boundary
passages.excerpt: “I am the true vine, and my Father is the farmer. Every branch in me that doesn’t bear fruit, he takes away. Every branch that bears fruit, he prunes, that it may bear more fruit. You a…
passages.observation: Jesus names himself as the true vine, his Father as farmer, and his followers as branches whose fruit depends on remaining in him.

passages.title: Christ bears sins on the tree
passages.phase: Life-giving plant images at the boundary
passages.excerpt: For you were called to this, because Christ also suffered for us, leaving you an example, that you should follow his steps, who didn’t sin, “neither was deceit found in his mouth.” When…
passages.observation: Peter says Christ suffered without retaliation, bore sins in his body on the tree, and brought straying people back to their Shepherd.

passages.title: The overcomer is promised the tree in Paradise
passages.excerpt: “To the angel of the assembly in Ephesus write: “He who holds the seven stars in his right hand, he who walks among the seven golden lamp stands says these things: “I know your works, a…
passages.observation: The message to Ephesus names labor, lost first love, repentance, and the Spirit’s promise of eating from the tree of life in God’s Paradise.

passages.title: The new creation removes death and pain
passages.excerpt: I saw a new heaven and a new earth, for the first heaven and the first earth have passed away, and the sea is no more. I saw the holy city, New Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from…
passages.observation: John sees new heaven, new earth, and the holy city; God dwells with people, wipes tears, and declares all things new.

passages.title: The city stands open yet excludes impurity
passages.excerpt: One of the seven angels who had the seven bowls which were loaded with the seven last plagues came, and he spoke with me, saying, “Come here. I will show you the bride, the Lamb’s wife.…
passages.observation: An angel shows the Lamb’s bride as a radiant city with gates, foundations, no temple, divine light, nations entering, and nothing unclean admitted.

passages.title: The tree bears fruit beside the river
passages.excerpt: He showed me a river of water of life, clear as crystal, proceeding out of the throne of God and of the Lamb, in the middle of its street. On this side of the river and on that was the…
passages.observation: The river of life flows from God and the Lamb’s throne; the tree of life bears monthly fruit and healing leaves, and servants see God’s face.

passages.title: The angel confirms the vision and corrects worship
passages.excerpt: He said to me, “These words are faithful and true. The Lord God of the spirits of the prophets sent his angel to show to his bondservants the things which must happen soon.” “Behold, I…
passages.observation: The angel calls the words faithful and true, announces that Jesus is coming soon, blesses the keeper, refuses John’s worship, and says not to seal the book.

passages.title: A blessing names the right to the tree
passages.excerpt: “Behold, I am coming soon! My reward is with me, to repay to each man according to his work. I am the Alpha and the Omega, the First and the Last, the Beginning and the End. Blessed are…
passages.observation: The coming speaker announces reward and identity; a blessing links doing the commandments with tree-of-life rights and city entrance.

passages.title: The final invitation and warning name life
passages.excerpt: The Spirit and the bride say, “Come!” He who hears, let him say, “Come!” He who is thirsty, let him come. He who desires, let him take the water of life freely. I testify to everyone wh…
passages.observation: The Spirit and bride invite the thirsty to take life-water freely; the book warns against adding or taking away and names loss from the tree and city.
